svg.title: What the second rewrite changed
svg.desc: The textual-memory profile after session 1 (91 words) and after session 2 (153 words), under the same four headings. The diet line was replaced, as the prompt asks: pescatarian since June 2026, previously strictly vegetarian since 2018, and the change is recorded again under 'Changes over time' as 2026-06-20. The allergy, cuisine and budget lines survived word for word. Lena, Jonas and their needs, Kreuzberg and the walking distance were added. Four changes nobody asked for are marked: 1, 'moved in May' became 'since 2026-05-01'; 2, 'can't eat shellfish' became 'has a shellfish allergy'; 3, the guess from session 1, 'based in or planning for Berlin', is kept as what the user said before; 4, the March dinner was dropped.
svg.text: The textual-memory profile after session 1, and after one LLM call rewrote all of it with session 2. The diet changed as the
prompt's rule asks; the four numbered changes are the rewriter's own.
Has a sister who is visiting Berlin.
Currently based in or planning for Berlin.
Prefers to spend no more than 40 euros per person for dining.
Planning a dinner for a sister's visit to Berlin, scheduled for
Sister named Lena; her partner is named Jonas.
Prefers to spend no more than 40 euros per person for dining.
Prefers restaurants within walking distance of Kreuzberg.
Sister (Lena) has a shellfish allergy; partner (Jonas) has
Planning a dinner for a visit from sister Lena and her partner,
previously based in or planning for Berlin generally).
“I moved to Kreuzberg in May” became “since 2026-05-01”: a
guessed day, written down as a date.
“Lena can't eat shellfish” became “has a shellfish allergy”. For a
booking it makes no difference; for a question about why, it does.
Kept its own guess as history
“Based in or planning for Berlin” was the rewriter's hedge in March.
In July it is recorded as what the user said before.
The March dinner is gone, replaced by the autumn visit. Here that is
right, but nothing outside the model checked it.
replaced, with the old value as history
From notebooks/01-textual.ipynb; each line without its bold label
